title: National Quality Framework for childcare (2012): re-evaluation with synthetic DiD
design: The framework started in January 2012 everywhere except WA (August 2012): 2011-12 childcare entry and exit in the seven early jurisdictions against WA, with synthetic DiD weights.
grade_reason: design checks passed; registered layer and checks agree
headline: No detectable effect: business entry rate −0.3 per 100 businesses a year (p = 0.85), synthetic DiD, grade Moderate.

category_summaries.competition: Business entry rate: −0.3 per 100 businesses a year (p = 0.85; detectable from 6.0). Business exit rate: −1.9 per 100 businesses a year (p = 0.049; detectable from 2.2).
category_summaries.prices: Child care: prices relative to the CPI: +4.4% (log points) (p = 0.075; detectable from 5.0).

key_insights: The question: did the National Quality Framework for childcare change how many childcare businesses opened or closed in its first year (2011-12)?
The comparison: The framework started in January 2012 everywhere except WA (August 2012): 2011-12 childcare entry and exit in the seven early jurisdictions against WA, with synthetic DiD weights.
What we found: no detectable change. Business entry rate: −0.3 per 100 businesses a year (90% interval −2.3 to +2.4; p = 0.85).

Other outcomes: business exit rate −1.9 (p = 0.049); child care: prices relative to the CPI +4.4 (p = 0.075). Secondary outcomes are outside the registered decision rule and not adjusted for testing several outcomes, so a p-value below 0.05 among them is a lead, not a finding.
How precise: only changes larger than about 6.0 per 100 businesses a year could have been detected.

Compared with the earlier evaluation (2026-10-15, now archived): it found no detectable effect (business entry rate −0.3 per 100 businesses a year). The conclusion is unchanged; the smallest detectable effect is now 6.0, down from 9.8. This evaluation uses the estimator chosen in the blinded power study and the latest data.
What it means: no effect is detectable with public state-level data; an effect smaller than the detectable size cannot be ruled out.

method.summary: Synthetic DiD on ANZSIC classes by state and financial year, the layer chosen for this reform in the blinded power study, with every other layer reported side by side.

equations.label: Synthetic DiD
equations.text: hat{τ} = arg min over (μ, α, β, τ) of Σ_{i,t} (y_{it} − μ − α_{i} − β_{t} − D_{it}·τ)^{2} · hat{ω}_{i} · hat{λ}_{t}

equations.label: Year by year
equations.text: y_{cst} = α_{cs} + δ_{ct} + γ_{st} + Σ_{k≠−1} β_{k}·1[t − T_{s} = k]·T_{cs} + ε_{cst}

terms.meaning: Entries (or exits) per 100 businesses operating at the start of year t, class c, state s
1 for the reform's class in a treated state (or city) from its first exposed period to the end of its window
weights on comparison cells, chosen so their pre-reform path matches the treated group's
weights on pre-reform periods, chosen to resemble the post-reform periods

method.estimand: The average change in the outcome for the reform's classes in treated states over the window, beyond the same classes elsewhere and the treated states' other classes, net of the mean placebo estimate.
method.identification: Without the reform, the treated classes in treated states would have moved like the same classes elsewhere plus their states' other classes (parallel trends in the saturated model; for synthetic DiD, like the weighted comparison cells).
method.inference: The same estimator applied to up to 40 placebo industry groups (or CPI classes) at the reform's states and dates gives the no-effect distribution: the p-value is the share of centred placebo estimates at least as large; the 90% interval subtracts their 5th and 95th percentiles. Benjamini-Hochberg q-values across the specification's primary outcomes. Placebo states and fake dates check the reform's own classes.
steps: Registered the layer, outcomes, windows and placebo pools in the specification before any treated post-reform outcome was computed.
Design stage: hid treated cells from first exposure, computed every layer's placebo distribution, the own-class placebos and the pre-reform event-study check.
Committed the design and plan, ran a blinded dry run, then one registered run with treated cells restored.
Judged the registered layer's estimate against its placebo distribution; reported every other layer side by side.

caveats: Moderate rather than Strong: the rule needs at least two cohorts, three treated states and a smallest detectable effect within 5; this design has 1 cohort, 7 treated states and a smallest detectable effect of 6.0.
Re-evaluation: the earlier results were known when this specification was written; the estimator layers were fixed beforehand by the blinded power study.
